name: quadcastrgb
desc: Set RGB lights on HyperX QuadCast S and Duocast microphones
why: Pokes the USB HID interface of a HyperX microphone to set its lights, a small hardware door.

brief.what_it_is: QuadcastRGB is a command-line program that sets the RGB lights on HyperX QuadCast S and DuoCast microphones, doing what the vendor's NGenuity software does. The homepage describes it as a "driver, if you wish," which suggests it talks to the mic directly rather than through a vendor service. The homepage does not show any command syntax, option list, or example output, so the inputs and exact light settings it accepts are not known from these notes. The executable is named quadcastrgb.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a way to control the lights on these mics without HyperX's NGenuity software, which is a Windows-oriented vendor app. The author says it is meant to work on all Unix-like systems.
brief.install_notes: The homepage offers prebuilt downloads: quadcastrgb 1.0.5 (May 26, 2025), quadcastrgb 1.0.4, a deb package for 1.0.4, and an rpm package for 1.0.4. The TODO list includes 'self-contained static compilation (without libusb)', which implies the current build depends on libusb. No first-run steps or permission setup are described on the homepage.
brief.standout: It is a small, single-purpose tool that reverse-engineers a consumer microphone's lighting control so it runs outside the vendor's software. The author says the Linux and macOS builds were tested on real hardware.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the homepage shows. The latest listed release is 1.0.5, dated May 26, 2025, and the TODO list reads like active planning. I could not see a commit history or a date for the last commit, so the exact activity level is uncertain.
brief.caveats: Tested only on Linux and macOS; FreeBSD is on the TODO list. The current build appears to depend on libusb, and a static build without it is not yet available. The foreground option (-f and --foreground) is not implemented yet. There is no visualizer or VU-meter mode, no save option, and no support for multiple mics. The homepage does not name a license. The homepage was reachable, but the README and the GitHub/GitLab mirror pages were not followed, so details beyond this page are unverified.
quotes: The program (or driver, if you wish) allows setting the RGB lights of HyperX Quadcast S and Duocast just like NGenuity does.
It is supposed to work on all Unix-like systems.
The Linux and MacOS versions have been tested and work as expected.
